issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for 'lectureName': the UML in the problem statement and the template expect lectureName to be a String, but the solution defines the field as a LectureName object (custom class). This divergence will confuse students about the expected type and can cause compilation/type errors when following the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the lectureName type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably change the solution to use a String for the lectureName field and constructor parameter (and remove or avoid using the LectureName wrapper class), or alternatively update the UML/problem statement and template to document and require the LectureName type consistently.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: the solution's Lecture constructor accepts a LectureName as the first parameter, whereas the problem UML and the template expect the lectureName parameter to be a String. This inconsistency will prevent students from implementing or instantiating Lecture in the straightforward way described by the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor signature with the UML: change the solution constructor to accept a String lectureName as the first parameter. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to require a LectureName parameter if the wrapper type is intentional, and ensure all artifacts and examples reflect that.

issues.description: Unexpected introduction of a new identifier (LectureName) in the solution: the solution adds a LectureName class and uses it for lectureName while the problem statement and template only reference a String. Introducing this new type without updating the exercise text or template can confuse students about whether they should create or use a LectureName class.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove the LectureName class from the solution and use a plain String for the lectureName throughout, or update the problem statement and template to introduce and require the LectureName type so students know to use or create that class. Ensure naming and types are consistent across all artifacts.
